text:
Alex Ng: Quick proposal — consolidate route_identity + derived_tags into a single route_profile (jsonb) + a small set of denorm cols (route_hash, tenant_id, p95_ms, p99_ms) so console queries stop joining 3 tables. Need an ingest compatibility + rollout playbook.
Priya Patel: What’s the main perf win? and is this mostly to help ad-hoc dashboard queries or the time-series ingest path? :thinking_face:
Dan Huang: Main risk is breaking existing route_id-based queries in the console and billing pipelines. Also need to check downstream analytics that expect separate attrs.
Maya Lopez: Suggestion: dual-write in the ingest path for 3 weeks, then shadow-backfill, then swap reads. Dual-write gives safe rollback.
Alex Ng: Agreed. Can we do a dual-write shim in the router layer where we populate route_profile and keep old fields? Example shim:
```\n// pseudo\nroute_profile = {\n  "route_id": route_id,\n  "labels": route_labels,\n  "derived": compute_derived(attrs)\n}\nINSERT INTO console_metrics (..., route_profile) VALUES (..., route_profile)\n// still write route_id, labels for compatibility\n```
Joel Park: For backfill we can run an idempotent UPDATE job: `UPDATE console_metrics SET route_profile = build_profile(route_id, labels) WHERE route_profile IS NULL;` run as paginated jobs by tenant shard. Keep cpu-parallelism low.
Priya Patel: Storage impact? duplicating fields will increase size — we should estimate. If avg row size grows 120 bytes and we have 2B rows, that’s significant. Maybe do compaction after we cutover.
Dan Huang: For queries that power per-route quotas we must ensure the canonical route_hash doesn’t change. We should derive route_hash deterministically from route_profile and keep old route_hash field until we promote.
migrations-bot: migration task created: MIG-2026-042: route_profile dual-write + backfill. Link: https://internal/tasks/MIG-2026-042 :white_check_mark:
Alex Ng: Canary strategy proposal: 1) dual-write + shadow backfill 2) enable read-path for 5% of console traffic (feature flag) 3) compare p95/p99 and row counts for 48h 4) expand to 25% then 100% if metrics within noise.
Maya Lopez: Operational notes: backfill should emit a progress stream to the console_ingest topic and a failure dead-letter queue. Keep the backfill job idempotent and resumable.
Joel Park: SQL for safety checks (run pre-cutover):
```\n-- compare p99 computed from old cols vs new route_profile\nSELECT route_hash, approx_percentile(old_latency_ms, 0.99) as old_p99, approx_percentile((route_profile->>'p99_ms')::double precision, 0.99) as new_p99\nFROM console_metrics\nWHERE route_profile IS NOT NULL\nGROUP BY route_hash\nHAVING abs(old_p99 - new_p99) > 50\nLIMIT 100\n```
Dan Huang: We should add a regression alert that fires if >1% of routes deviate by >100ms after cutover. Also validate quota accounting: compare computed_quota_cost(old) vs computed_quota_cost(new) for a sample.
Priya Patel: Regarding storage, we can GC old columns after 30 days post-promote, but only after verifying historical queries and billing reports use the new shape. Schedule a delayed compaction window.
Alex Ng: TL;DR actions: [@Maya] build dual-write shim + feature flag, [@Joel] backfill runner + safety SQL, [@Priya] storage/size estimate and compaction plan, [@Dan] quota/identity validation tests. I’ll own rollout playbook and postmortem template.
sre-bot: Note: rolling back a schema change that increases row width will require a migration throughput cap on write nodes. Plan maintenance window if compaction/GC touches many partitions.
Maya Lopez: Will start the shim PR today, will include config to toggle dual-write per-tenant.
Joel Park: I’ll draft the backfill job with pagination tokens and DLQ hooks, aim for a dry-run mode next week.
Priya Patel: I’ll run a quick size delta estimate with sampled partitions and share numbers by EOD.
Alex Ng: Thanks — capturing this for MIG-2026-042. If folks can +1 the plan once they’ve reviewed the PRs we’ll schedule the canary. :thumbsup:
Dan Huang: +1
Maya Lopez: +1
Joel Park: +1
Priya Patel: +1
